---
title: "GitHub workflow"
---

## Complete GitHub workflow

In this assignment, you will configure Git, commit changes, and create an issue on GitHub.

## Step 1: Introduce yourself to git

1. In Posit Cloud, open the md-01-assignments-USERNAME project that ends with your GitHub username.

![](images/screenshot-posit-cloud-project.png){width=100%}

2. Open the git-configuration.qmd file from the bottom right window of RStudio.

![](images/screenshot-rstudio-files-pane.png){width=100%}

3. Edit the code chunk under the heading **Git configuration** and replace the placeholders with your name and email address (these will be the details that git will use to identify you when you make changes to your work). 

![](images/screenshot-git-config-code.png){width=100%}
4. Render the document by clicking the "Render" button at the top of the file.

![](images/screenshot-render-button.png){width=100%}

5. Continue with the next step

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(usethis)

# Replace Your Name and Your Email with your details. Do not delete the quotes "".
use_git_config(user.name = "Your Name", user.email = "Your Email")
```

## Step 2: Commit and push your changes

1. Navigate to the Git pane in the top-right window of RStudio

![](images/screenshot-rstudio-git-pane.png){width=100%}

2. Check the box next to the git-configuration.qmd file to stage it for commit

![](images/screenshot-git-stage-file.png){width=100%}

3. Click on the "Commit" button

![](images/screenshot-git-commit-button.png){width=100%}

4. Enter a commit message in the "Commit message" field

![](images/screenshot-git-commit-message.png){width=100%}

5. Click on the "Commit" button

![](images/screenshot-git-commit-confirm.png){width=100%}

6. Click on the "Push" button

![](images/screenshot-git-push-button.png){width=100%}

7. Enter your GitHub username and GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) in the "Username" and "Password" fields

![](images/screenshot-git-credentials.png){width=100%}

::: callout-important
## Do not use your GitHub password

You need to enter the GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) you created in the previous assignment to push your changes back to GitHub.
:::

## Step 3: Open an issue on GitHub

1. Open [github.com](https://github.com/) in your browser.

![](images/screenshot-github-homepage-2.png){width=100%}

2. Navigate to the GitHub organisation for the course.

![](images/screenshot-github-org.png){width=100%}

3. Find the repository md-01-assignments that ends with your GitHub username.

![](images/screenshot-github-your-repo.png){width=100%}

4. Click on the "Issues" tab.

![](images/screenshot-github-issues-tab.png){width=100%}

5. Click on the green "New issue" button.

![](images/screenshot-github-new-issue.png){width=100%}

6. In the "Title" field write: "Completed module 1 assignments".

![](images/screenshot-github-issue-title.png){width=100%}

7. In the "Leave a comment" field, tag the course instructors @larnsce @mianzg @sskorik01

![](images/screenshot-github-issue-comment.png){width=100%}

8. Click "Submit new issue"

![](images/screenshot-github-submit-issue.png){width=100%}

Congratulations! You have completed the GitHub workflow assignments.
